head: No collateral.
No problem.
slides.sub: How a bank for the poorest women spread worldwide.

image.label: Women gathered in a Bangladeshi village courtyard
image.brief: 1970년대 말 방글라데시 시골 마을 안마당에 사리를 입은 여성들이 둥글게 앉아 있는 장면. 따뜻한 아침 햇살, 흙벽과 야자수. 얼굴은 특정되지 않게 원경이나 뒷모습으로. 로고 없음.

head: An economics professor
in a famine.
body: In 1974, famine struck Bangladesh. Muhammad Yunus was teaching economics at Chittagong University, near hungry villages.
He later said the elegant theories in his lectures felt useless. So he started walking into the village of Jobra to see how people actually lived.

image.label: A university building beside dry rice fields
image.brief: 1970년대 방글라데시 대학 건물과 그 옆으로 펼쳐진 메마른 논. 대비되는 두 세계. 인물은 멀리 작은 실루엣으로만.

head: She worked all day.
The lender kept the profit.
body: Yunus met women who made bamboo stools. They had no money for bamboo, so they borrowed from traders and moneylenders on harsh terms.
After repaying, they kept only a few cents a day. They were trapped by tiny sums.

image.label: Hands weaving a bamboo stool
image.brief: 흙바닥 위에서 대나무 의자를 엮는 손 클로즈업. 거친 손, 대나무 조각, 부드러운 자연광.

slides.label: lent to 42 women, in a story he has often told
body: Yunus listed everyone in Jobra who depended on lenders. The total they needed was about $27. He lent it from his own pocket, and they paid him back.

image.label: A few coins and notes on a handwritten list
image.brief: 손으로 쓴 이름 목록 위에 놓인 몇 장의 지폐와 동전. 방글라데시 화폐 느낌이지만 실제 지폐 디자인은 그대로 그리지 않음.

head: The banks said no.
He signed for them.
body: Yunus asked banks to lend to the poor. They refused: no collateral, no credit history, and many borrowers could not read the forms.
So he guaranteed the loans himself. The money came back. Still, he could not personally sign for a whole country.

image.label: A man at a bank counter facing a closed window
image.brief: 1970년대 방글라데시 은행 창구. 서류 더미와 닫힌 창구 앞에 선 남성의 뒷모습 실루엣.

head: No collateral, no records.
How do you lend safely?
body: You want to reach thousands of poor villagers. Banks won't take the risk, and you can't guarantee every loan yourself.

options.text: Lend to small groups who vouch for each other and repay weekly
options.feedback: Cheap to run and relies on neighbors, but needs strong group discipline. Keep swiping.

options.text: Give grants instead, since the poor can't be expected to repay
options.feedback: It helps right away, but the money runs out and doesn't grow. Keep swiping.

options.text: Accept small collateral, like jewelry or livestock
options.feedback: It feels safer, but it shuts out the people with nothing. Keep swiping.

image.label: A crossroads on a village path
image.brief: 마을 흙길이 세 갈래로 갈라지는 장면. 이른 아침 안개.

head: Collateral was replaced
by neighbors.
body: Borrowers joined groups of five. Each member's chance at a loan depended on the group's record, so friends chose each other carefully and nudged anyone falling behind.
Loans were small, repaid in weekly installments at village meetings, so no one faced one big payment.

image.label: Five women seated together with a ledger
image.brief: 다섯 명의 여성이 둘러앉아 장부를 함께 보는 장면. 얼굴은 특정되지 않게 측면이나 그림자로.

slides.label: of borrowers are women, according to the bank
body: Over time, Grameen focused on women. Yunus argued they repaid reliably and spent earnings on children and homes. A bank had chosen the customers every other bank ignored.

image.label: A woman selling goods at a small village stall
image.brief: 마을 작은 좌판에서 물건을 파는 여성의 뒷모습. 바구니, 닭, 채소. 활기 있는 장터 분위기.

head: A village project
became a global model.
body: In 1983, a government ordinance made Grameen an independent bank, mostly owned by its borrowers. Microlenders around the world copied its methods.
In 2006, Yunus and the bank shared the Nobel Peace Prize. Critics later questioned interest rates and over-borrowing, but the idea had spread.

image.label: A world map dotted with small lights
image.brief: 작은 불빛들이 여러 대륙에 점점이 퍼져 나가는 세계 지도 그래픽. 방글라데시에서 시작되는 느낌.

head: Ask what collateral is for.
Then replace it.
body: Banks used collateral to manage risk. Yunus went back to first principles: what they really needed was information and a reason to repay.
Small groups supplied both. That opened a market of customers banks had treated as impossible to serve.

image.label: A padlock dissolving into linked hands
image.brief: 자물쇠가 서로 맞잡은 손들로 바뀌어 가는 그래픽. 단순한 선, 따뜻한 색.

head: Your customers aren't risky.
Your rules might be.
body: Industry rules often exist to solve one problem. Solve that problem another way, and new customers appear.
**Try it today:** list one rule that blocks customers from buying from you. What is it really protecting, and how else could you protect it?

image.label: An open door to a sunlit village
image.brief: 열린 문 너머로 햇살 가득한 방글라데시 마을이 보이는 구도.

factChecks.note: 1974년 방글라데시 기근과 Muhammad Yunus가 당시 치타공 대학 경제학 교수였다는 점은 노벨위원회 자료와 Yunus의 자서전 『Banker to the Poor』(1999)로 확인하세요.
조브라(Jobra) 마을에서 자기 돈 27달러를 여성 42명에게 빌려줬다는 이야기는 Yunus 본인이 자서전 등에서 반복해 전한 일화입니다. 카드에는 "a story he has often told"로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] Yunus의 첫 대출 27달러 확인. 여성 42명은 이번 검색에서 미확인(자서전 일화).
Yunus가 초기에 Janata Bank 등 국영 은행 대출에 개인 보증을 섰다는 내용은 『Banker to the Poor』와 Grameen Bank 연혁으로 확인하세요.
1983년 정부 법령(Grameen Bank Ordinance)으로 독립 은행이 된 시점과, 대출자가 은행 지분 대부분을 소유한다는 점은 Grameen Bank 공식 자료 기준입니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1983년 10월 정식 은행 전환 확인.
대출자 중 여성 비율 "약 97%"는 회사 발표 수치입니다. 시기에 따라 달라지므로 최신 공식 자료로 확인하고 카드에는 "according to the bank"로 표시했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2008년 5월 대출자 750만 명 중 97% 여성 확인.
5인 그룹·주간 상환 구조는 초기 그라민 모델(이른바 Grameen I) 기준입니다. 상환율은 측정 방식 논란(2001년 Wall Street Journal 보도 등)이 있어 구체적 수치를 넣지 않았습니다.
2006년 노벨평화상을 Yunus와 Grameen Bank가 공동 수상한 사실은 노벨위원회 발표로 확인하세요. 이후 이자율·과잉 대출 비판도 있어 카드에 짧게 언급했습니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 2006년 노벨평화상 공동 수상 확인.
